chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muramim, who said:
Al-Fuqqah (a type of bread) was prepared for Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) in his house.
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya said: Abu Ahmad (meaning Ibn Abi Umayr) said: And Fuqqah is not prepared if it boils.
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan is the one who clarifies what Ibn Abi Umayr mentioned.

key_terms.أَبُو أَحْمَدَ: A reference to Ibn Abi Umayr, used here to clarify the narrator chain.
key_terms.الْفُقَّاعُ: A type of bread or flatbread, often associated with specific preparation methods in hadith literature.
key_terms.يَغْلِي: It boils; referring to the state of the bread or dough during preparation.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on preparing Fuqqah (bread) if it boils according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* highlights the practical application of purity laws in the domestic sphere of the Imams, specifically regarding the preparation of *al-Fuqqah* (a type of flatbread or cake). The chain of narration clarifies a technical distinction: while the bread is prepared in Imam al-Hassan’s (AS) house, it is deemed invalid if it boils, a detail that underscores the rigorous attention to ritual cleanliness (*taharah*) in Shia culinary and domestic practices.
